rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Reasons under San Francisco Rent Ordinance Section 37.9(a)
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a just cause reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing eviction from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance. There are 17 specified just cause reasons including non-payment of rent, substantial lease breach, nuisance, illegal use, refusal to renew lease, refusal to allow landlord access, unauthorized subtenant, owner-occupancy, condominium conversion, demolition, capital improvements, substantial rehabilitation, Ellis Act withdrawal, lead remediation, development agreements, Good Samaritan tenancy expiration, and development project demolition.
rules.summary_plain: In San Francisco, a landlord can only evict a tenant for one of 17 specific just cause reasons listed in the Rent Ordinance. Expiration of a lease or change in ownership alone is not enough.
rules.summary_plain_es: En San Francisco, un propietario solo puede desalojar a un inquilino por una de las 17 razones específicas de causa justa enumeradas en la Ordenanza de Alquiler. La expiración de un contrato de arrendamiento o el cambio de propietario por sí solos no son suficientes.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance, including some units exempt from rent increase limits but still subject to eviction provisions.
rules.exemptions_text: Tenancies in newly constructed rental units with Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible under Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, and some rent-regulated tenancies by other agencies are exempt from rent increase limits but still subject to just cause eviction provisions.
rules.penalty: Landlords who unlawfully evict or attempt to evict tenants may face substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
